n67facc00ab.headline: G20's financial watchdog lays out climate plan but presses pause amid divisions
n67facc00ab.summary: The G20's Financial Stability Board delivered a new plan on tackling climate-related financial risks but paused further policy work. The pause follows a retreat by the United States.
n67facc00ab.why: The Financial Stability Board coordinates global financial regulation for the G20, and its standards shape how banks and insurers manage climate risk.

n52a00d76cb.headline: GBP/USD Forecast: Sterling Extends Losses After Soft GDP Data
n52a00d76cb.summary: Sterling extended losses after the UK released downbeat GDP data in the previous session. The GBP/USD pair continued its decline.
n52a00d76cb.why: Sterling is the British pound, and its value reflects UK growth, interest-rate expectations and trade flows.

n4880af7be0.headline: Stellantis trying to save key supplier CLN – reports
n4880af7be0.summary: Steel components supplier CLN is struggling to stay in business, according to reports. Stellantis wants to secure the future of a major supplier.
n4880af7be0.why: Stellantis is one of the world's largest carmakers, and disruption at key suppliers can affect vehicle production schedules.

impacts.name: Stellantis
impacts.why: Stellantis depends on steel component suppliers, and its efforts to secure CLN's future relate to that supply chain.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

n420c67b960.headline: Azerbaijan reveals volume of daily oil production
n420c67b960.summary: Azerbaijan's daily oil production, including condensate, was reported for June 2025. The figure in the source is incomplete.
n420c67b960.why: Azerbaijan is an oil and gas producer whose output feeds into Caspian and European energy supply. Production levels influence regional export revenues.

n1eb05f0f5c.headline: Spaniards struggle to enjoy their own beaches in tourist deluge
n1eb05f0f5c.summary: International holidaymakers are keeping Spaniards off their own beaches as hotel and rental prices rise during an unprecedented tourism boom, Reuters reports.
n1eb05f0f5c.why: Tourism is a major part of Spain's economy, and rising accommodation prices affect hospitality companies, property rentals and domestic consumer spending.

n578a874480.headline: Tesco Bank issues 'concerning' warning to three million customers
n578a874480.summary: Tesco Bank, which has three million customers, said a 'concerning' study found people are unaware they are losing money.
n578a874480.why: Tesco Bank is the financial services arm of the UK grocer Tesco, offering current accounts, credit cards and loans.

nb962def21f.headline: Trump's tariff threat to Brazil stands out for import tax amount and personal tone
nb962def21f.summary: Of more than two dozen tariff threat letters sent by President Trump, the one to Brazil proposed the highest import tax and had a personal tone. The letter targets Brazilian imports.
nb962def21f.why: Brazil is a major exporter of commodities and manufactured goods to the United States, so US import tariffs directly affect its trade flows and growth.

na59aea6f94.headline: Trump sets new ultimatum for Putin: 'Maybe he'll start negotiating'
na59aea6f94.summary: President Donald Trump announced he has given Russian President Vladimir Putin a new 50-day deadline. Trump said Putin may start negotiating.
na59aea6f94.why: Russia is a major energy and commodity exporter, so progress or breakdown in talks can affect energy prices and sanctions risk.

n2168c32fd9.headline: GLOBAL MARKETS-Equities Rise Modestly with Tariffs, Inflation Data, Earnings in Focus
n2168c32fd9.summary: MSCI's global stock gauge rose 0.90 points, or 0.10%, to 923.46, with investors on edge over US tariff threats while focusing on inflation data and earnings.
n2168c32fd9.why: The MSCI All Country World Index tracks large and mid-cap stocks across developed and emerging markets, making it a broad gauge of global equity sentiment.

nd11084bb08.headline: Greek Stocks Drop Slightly Amid Trade War Fears
nd11084bb08.summary: Greek stocks fell 0.34% as European markets reacted negatively to US trade tariffs. The move was a small decline in the Athens market.
nd11084bb08.why: The Athens Stock Exchange is Greece's main equity market, and its index reflects the performance of major Greek listed companies such as banks and utilities.

nde8361d192.headline: Indian stock market falls amid fresh US tariff threats, selling in IT stock
nde8361d192.summary: The Indian stock market ended the first session of the week lower on Monday, amid selling in IT stocks and fresh global trade tariff threats from the US.
nde8361d192.why: The Indian benchmark indices track the country's largest listed companies, and IT exporters are sensitive to US trade policy.
nde8361d192.why_moved: Selling in IT stocks and fresh US tariff threats weighed on the market at the start of the week.

n1c62b24718.headline: Gold eases after hitting three-week high
n1c62b24718.summary: Gold prices edged lower after reaching a three-week high on Monday, with attention on trade talks and US economic data, while silver rose to its highest since September 2011.
n1c62b24718.why: Gold and silver are widely used as stores of value and hedges, and their prices reflect inflation expectations, rates and risk sentiment.

n849dfae76b.headline: U.S. markets open week with modest decline
n849dfae76b.summary: U.S. stock markets opened the week slightly lower as investors reacted to fresh trade threats from President Donald Trump and awaited key economic data and corporate earnings.
n849dfae76b.why: U.S. equity indexes such as the S&P 500 reflect expectations for corporate profits, trade policy and the economy, which drive global risk sentiment.

n34548b0210.headline: France to quicken defense-spending boost in bid to be ‘feared’
n34548b0210.summary: France will quicken its defence-spending boost to become more feared, Macron told troops and officers in Paris. He said the nuclear deterrent is sovereign and plays a role in European security.
n34548b0210.why: Defence budgets shape government spending and the order books of defence contractors. European rearmament is a major theme for investors in the sector.

nb4f5117435.headline: Renewable energy delays make Australia less attractive
nb4f5117435.summary: A study rates investment in Australian renewable energy as only somewhat attractive, citing delays tied to transmission and planning.
nb4f5117435.why: Renewable project pipelines depend on grid transmission and planning approvals, which affect returns for energy investors.

nc6cb40cfb0.headline: HVS Asia Pacific Hospitality Newsletter - Week Ending 11 July 2025
nc6cb40cfb0.summary: United Urban Investment will acquire the Smile Hotel Premium Osaka Honmachi in Japan for JPY8.69 billion, according to the Hospitality Net weekly newsletter.
nc6cb40cfb0.why: United Urban is a Japanese real estate investment trust that owns hotels and commercial properties, so acquisitions affect its portfolio and income.

n25f41dccef.headline: Kesoram Industries' Q1 loss widens to Rs 99.3 crore, revenue drops 9.3 pc YoY
n25f41dccef.summary: Kolkata-based Kesoram Industries reported a wider consolidated net loss of Rs 99.3 crore for Q1 FY26, with revenue down 9.3% year on year.
n25f41dccef.why: Kesoram Industries is an Indian conglomerate with interests in cement, tyres and textiles, and its results reflect those sectors' conditions.

n9f06eb9413.headline: Wisconsin still losing out from not expanding Medicaid — even under Trump’s big bill
n9f06eb9413.summary: Wisconsin has missed out on $2.6 billion in Medicaid funding because it did not expand the program. The state will still be subject to new work requirements under Trump's big bill.
n9f06eb9413.why: Medicaid funding affects state budgets, healthcare providers and insurers. Federal health policy changes can shift costs between states and the federal government.

nb5e0ce167a.headline: India's retail inflation falls to over 6-year low of 2.1 pc in June
nb5e0ce167a.summary: India's Consumer Price Index inflation eased further to 2.1% in June, according to the report. The figure is described as a more than six-year low.
nb5e0ce167a.why: Consumer price inflation is a key input for the Reserve Bank of India's interest rate decisions, which shape borrowing costs and equity valuations.

nf8958fcf67.headline: Fitch Solutions: Azerbaijan gains opportunity to increase its share in the EU gas market
nf8958fcf67.summary: A Fitch Solutions report, cited by APA-Economics, says Azerbaijan has an opportunity to increase its share of the European Union gas market.
nf8958fcf67.why: Europe's gas imports are a key driver of energy security and pricing, and supplier shares shape long-term gas trade flows.

nd1e81d5626.headline: Government needs to overhaul ‘unfair’ business rates, says Greene King boss
nd1e81d5626.summary: Greene King chief executive Nick Mackenzie said the government needs to overhaul business rates, which he called unfair, and reduce property tax payments to drive investment and jobs.
nd1e81d5626.why: Greene King is a UK pub company, and business rates are a significant property cost for hospitality operators, affecting their investment and hiring.

n2eb2ce124c.headline: Political tensions muddy PM's Chinese green steel push
n2eb2ce124c.summary: Efforts to end Chinese ownership of an Australian port highlight challenges to the prime minister's ambition to grow green steel.
n2eb2ce124c.why: Chinese ownership of strategic infrastructure and green steel ambitions both affect Australia's trade and industrial investment outlook.

ne01077176e.headline: More than 2,000 pubs have closed in Ireland in past 20 years, report says
ne01077176e.summary: Pub closures in Ireland have averaged about 112 a year over the past two decades, rising to 128 annually between 2019 and 2024, according to a report.
ne01077176e.why: Pubs and hospitality are a major part of Ireland's consumer services sector. Closure trends reflect pressures on consumer spending, costs and property values in the sector.

nd16e15e534.headline: China’s Economy Set to Slow in Q2 as Pressure from US Tariffs Mounts
nd16e15e534.summary: China's economy is likely to have cooled in the second quarter after a solid start, as trade tensions and a prolonged property downturn weigh on demand. Policymakers face pressure for more stimulus.
nd16e15e534.why: China is the world's second-largest economy, so its growth trajectory affects global commodity demand, trade flows and emerging-market investors.

ncbed065451.headline: Allies under fire: Why do Trump tariffs target Korea, Japan first?
ncbed065451.summary: US President Donald Trump took aim at South Korea and Japan, catching both countries off guard. The move dashed expectations of protection for the two Asian allies.
ncbed065451.why: Tariffs on major Asian trading partners affect export-dependent manufacturers and currencies across the region.

n74ac9ceef1.headline: Two biggest railway unions reject pay offer, more strikes loom
n74ac9ceef1.summary: Members of the two largest Dutch railway unions rejected an improved pay offer from train operator NS. Further strikes are now feared after four regional strikes in June.
n74ac9ceef1.why: NS is the Dutch national rail operator, and prolonged labour disputes can disrupt transport services and add cost pressure.

ncbe1491642.headline: Tuesday preview: US CPI, Q2 results in focus
ncbe1491642.summary: Investors will focus on the latest US cost-of-living data due out on Tuesday. Second-quarter company results are also on the agenda.
ncbe1491642.why: Inflation data such as the US consumer price index influences expectations for Federal Reserve interest-rate decisions, which move bond and equity markets.

n3bd5d9c226.headline: EU Plans Tariffs on $72B US Goods Over Trade Dispute
n3bd5d9c226.summary: The European Union is preparing retaliatory tariffs on $72 billion of US exports amid escalating trade tensions, according to Commissioner Sefcovic. The measures respond to an ongoing trade dispute.
n3bd5d9c226.why: The EU is the largest trading bloc in the world, and tariff escalation between it and the US affects exporters, supply chains and currency markets.
n3bd5d9c226.why_moved: Escalating tariff threats on trade flows between the EU and US raise uncertainty for exporters and global supply chains.

nba49bc2840.headline: Australia urged to make 'gutsy' call against China war
nba49bc2840.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will raise Australian concerns over Chinese steel dumping. He is urging industry leaders from both countries to develop low-carbon steel production methods.
nba49bc2840.why: Steel dumping, where exports are sold below cost, can hurt domestic steelmakers and trade balances. Low-carbon steel is a growing area of investment as industry decarbonises.

n26fa8a1468.headline: South Korea's ICT exports rise 5.8 pc in H1 2025 on global chip demand
n26fa8a1468.summary: South Korea's exports of information and communication technology products rose 5.8% in the first half from a year earlier. The increase was driven by global chip demand.
n26fa8a1468.why: South Korea is a major exporter of memory chips and electronics, so its export data is a closely watched gauge of global tech demand.

n30cda384d6.headline: Markets decline in early trade dragged by IT stocks, foreign fund outflows
n30cda384d6.summary: Indian markets declined in early trade, dragged by IT stocks and foreign fund outflows. Bajaj Finance, Infosys, Tech Mahindra, Bharti Airtel, HCL Tech and Asian Paints were among the biggest laggards.
n30cda384d6.why: Foreign institutional flows and large IT exporters such as Infosys strongly influence the direction of India's benchmark equity indices.
n30cda384d6.why_moved: Selling in IT stocks and outflows by foreign funds dragged the market lower in early trade.

n2f8a41f708.headline: Current account deficit shrinks by $5.68b in 11 months of FY25
n2f8a41f708.summary: Bangladesh's current account deficit stood at $432 million in July-May of FY25, according to Bangladesh Bank. That is sharply lower than the $6.12 billion deficit in the same period of FY24.
n2f8a41f708.why: The current account balance measures a country's trade and transfers with the world and affects its foreign reserves and currency stability.

n46ffc6eb70.headline: Dollar hits 15-week high against yen as consumer prices gain
n46ffc6eb70.summary: The dollar reached a 15-week high against the yen on Tuesday after US consumer prices rose by the most in five months in June. Traders also pared expectations for Federal Reserve rate cuts.
n46ffc6eb70.why: The dollar-yen rate reflects the gap between US and Japanese interest rates and moves on US inflation and Fed policy expectations.
n46ffc6eb70.why_moved: A larger rise in US consumer prices led traders to pare expectations for Fed rate cuts, supporting the dollar.

nb3eb5ebcc1.headline: China is buying appliances and iPhones. What happens when the subsidies stop?
nb3eb5ebcc1.summary: Shoppers are using a US$42 billion trade-in subsidy programme to buy appliances and iPhones. Some cities have begun to cut back on the subsidies in recent weeks.
nb3eb5ebcc1.why: Consumer spending is a major driver of China's economy, and subsidy programmes influence retail demand for electronics and appliances.

nd8d8030551.headline: Ottawa is asking Canadians what they want to see in the fall budget
nd8d8030551.summary: Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne is seeking feedback on national security, defence spending and strengthening the economy. The budget comes amid an ongoing trade war.
nd8d8030551.why: The federal budget sets government spending and tax policy, which influence fiscal deficits, borrowing and economic growth.

n4bd6fb7c73.headline: Liquefied Gas Has Sharply Risen in Price in Armenia
n4bd6fb7c73.summary: Liquefied gas prices have risen sharply in Armenia. Radio Free Europe reports the increase is not explained by domestic market fluctuations, with causes sought across the Armenian-Georgian border.
n4bd6fb7c73.why: Liquefied petroleum gas is a household and industrial fuel, so price changes feed into consumer costs and inflation.

nd0e8aa4708.headline: AZERTAC: Authorities report oil production in Azerbaijan in the first half of the year
nd0e8aa4708.summary: Azerbaijan produced 13.7 million tonnes of oil, including condensate, in January–June 2025, 4.86% less than a year earlier. The Azeri-Chirag-Gunashli field produced 8 million tonnes.
nd0e8aa4708.why: Azerbaijan is an oil exporter whose output levels affect the Caspian crude supply that feeds into Mediterranean and European markets.
